findings.item: Family 002 (The full BSD formula from low Selmer corank) has NO Lean artifact. lean/docs/002.md does not exist; formalization.yaml main_results (lines 972-1771) contains no entry whose file is under OAI/NumberTheory relating to BSD/Selmer; no ComparatorChallenges/*.json names it. history.md (2026-10-07 'Fixes') only records for it: 'Exact Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer Formula from Low Selmer Corank: removed an obsolete introductory citation to a removed supporting manuscript.' CONTENTS.md line 32 describes 002 as proving full BSD + finiteness of Sha for curves with q^infinity-Selmer corank 0 or 1 for some prime q, and line 141 describes companion 006 (Goldfeld) which also has no Lean. Kill test K-RANK2: even if 002 were Lean-checked it could not apply to E (every p^infinity-Selmer corank >= 2); it could at most apply to E^{-7} (corank 0, where GZK already gives rank 0 and Sha finite).
findings.why_relevant: Confirms the expected negative: the only openai/math family about BSD/Selmer is unformalized, so nothing in the Lean tree can lift any seed obligation (FIN, ORDER9, Q36, Sha[p^infinity]) above IMPORTED_PREPRINT grade.

findings.item: No formalized statement about Selmer groups, Tate-Shafarevich groups, Galois cohomology, modular forms, Hecke operators, Heegner points, Iwasawa theory or BSD exists anywhere in lean/OAI (23,530 .lean files under OAI/NumberTheory, 103,000+ overall). A regex sweep for EllipticCurve|WeierstrassCurve|Selmer|Tate.Shafarevich|Iwasawa|ModularForm|CuspForm|GaloisCohomology|Heegner|BirchSwinnerton hits only 10 files, all in OAI/NumberTheory/SingleFold/ (plus false-positive 'Catalan/Determinants/FixedCanonicalBaseModRow*.lean' matching 'BSD'-free substrings). The NumberTheory subfolders are: Catalan, Chromatic, CubicGauss, CubicGram, CubicMoment, DirichletL, DuffinSchaeffer, DukePrimeDegree, EgyptianFractions, GaussianMoat, Jacobsthal, JointDickman, NumberField, OrdinaryCorrelations, Ostmann, PiExponent, PowerFree, PrimeGaps, PrimePackets, QuadraticForms, ShortEgyptian, SiegelZeros, SingleFold, TotientAsymptotic, TotientFibers, TwoPoint, TwoPointCorrelations, ZetaFive.
findings.why_relevant: Answers task item (b): refutes nothing, confirms the expectation that no Selmer/Galois-cohomology/modular/Iwasawa object is formalized; the lab's LEAN_CHECKED grading cannot import any such statement from this repository.

findings.item: The ONLY elliptic-curve arithmetic in Lean in the whole repository is an uncatalogued supporting module inside family 242 (Single-fold Diophantine representations): a complete 2-descent on the congruent-number curve E: y^2 = x^3 - 25x over Q using Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve.Affine API. Verbatim declarations: OAI/NumberTheory/SingleFold/DescentMap.lean: 'abbrev E : WeierstrassCurve.Affine ℚ := ⟨0,0,0,-25,0⟩', 'noncomputable def kummer : E.Point →+ Additive SquareClass × Additive SquareClass' (line 311), 'theorem kummer_eq_zero_iff (P : E.Point) : kummer P = 0 ↔ ∃ Q : E.Point, (2:ℕ) • Q=P' (line 319); OAI/NumberTheory/SingleFold/Torsion.lean line 88: 'theorem torsion_iff (P : E.Point) : IsOfFinAddOrder P ↔ (2:ℕ) • P = 0'; OAI/NumberTheory/SingleFold/Rank.lean line 336: 'theorem rank_one : ∃ (T : Type) (_ : AddCommGroup T) (_ : Finite T), Nonempty (E.Point ≃+ (Fin 1 → ℤ) × T)' with generator 'def G : E.Point := some (25/4) (75/8) ...' (line 303) and local-descent lemmas at p=5 in LocalDescent.lean ('mod_five_anisotropic', 'no_norm_five_int'). Not listed in formalization.yaml or docs/242.md (which only names the comparator target OAI.SingleFold.main : MainStatement, ComparatorChallenges/SingleFold.lean). No sorry in the SingleFold folder.
findings.why_relevant: Closest existing Lean template for what the lab's Lean capstone could realistically state about the seed: a Mathlib-WeierstrassCurve-level formalization of a 2-descent (E(Q)/2E(Q) via a Kummer map into square classes, torsion = 2-torsion). The seed's recorded facts 'E(Q)_tors = Z/2' and 'Sha(E/Q)[2] = 0, rank 2' are 2-descent facts of the same shape, but this code is for a different, CM, rank-1 curve with full rational 2-torsion; the seed curve has only one rational 2-torsion point (0,0), so the Kummer map would need the quartic/2-isogeny descent, which this module does not contain. Mathlib itself has no Selmer group, so Sha[2]=0 could only be encoded as an explicit statement about E(Q)/2E(Q) and local solubility. Unrefereed AI-generated code: usable only as a pattern, never as an imported result.

findings.item: Family 003 (The quasi-Riemann hypothesis + Uniform exclusion of Landau-Siegel zeros) is the only L-function family with Lean. Exact comparator declarations (each comparator .lean is the statement with 'sorry'; the solutions live in OAI/NumberTheory/DirichletL/Nonvanishing.lean, OAI/NumberTheory/DirichletL/Hecke/Nonvanishing.lean, OAI/NumberTheory/SiegelZeros/Conclusions/Theorem.lean, 0 sorry): (i) ComparatorChallenges/QuasiRiemannHypothesis.lean: 'theorem riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_seven_eighths_lt_re {s : ℂ} (hs : (7 / 8 : ℝ) < s.re) : riemannZeta s ≠ 0' (decl OAI.riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_seven_eighths_lt_re; config QuasiRiemannHypothesis.json: solution_module OAI.NumberTheory.DirichletL.Nonvanishing, permitted_axioms propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice, enable_nanoda false); (ii) DirichletSevenEighths.lean: 'theorem LFunction_ne_zero_of_seven_eighths_lt_re {q : ℕ} [NeZero q] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q) {s : ℂ} (hs : (7 / 8 : ℝ) < s.re) (hpole : ¬ (χ = 1 ∧ s = 1)) : _root_.DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ s ≠ 0' (decl OAI.DirichletCharacter.LFunction_ne_zero_of_seven_eighths_lt_re); (iii) HeckeSevenEighths.lean: 'theorem LFunction_ne_zero_of_seven_eighths_lt_re (χ : Character) {s : ℂ} (hs : (7 / 8 : ℝ) < s.re) (hpole : ¬ (χ.residue = 1 ∧ s = 1)) : LFunction χ s ≠ 0' where 'abbrev K := CyclotomicField 3 ℚ', Character is a finite-order ray-class-type character on O_K with unit_trivial, and 'LFunction χ s := continuedLattice χ s / 6' is a hand-built theta-series Mellin transform (decl OAI.SevenEighths.HeckeFamily.LFunction_ne_zero_of_seven_eighths_lt_re, file OAI/NumberTheory/DirichletL/Hecke/Nonvanishing.lean); (iv) SiegelZeros.lean: 'theorem exists_absolute_real_zero_gap : ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ (q : ℕ) [NeZero q], 3 ≤ q → ∀ χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, χ.IsPrimitive → χ ≠ 1 → (∀ a : ZMod q, (χ a).im = 0) → ∀ β : ℝ, 0 < β → β < 1 → χ.LFunction (β : ℂ) = 0 → c ≤ (1 - β) * Real.log (q : ℝ)' (decl OAI.SiegelZeros.WeightedTorusJets.exists_absolute_real_zero_gap). docs/003.md scope: 'The paper's later applications are not included'; 'No explicit value of c is given'. The Hecke statement is over Q(sqrt(-3)) only, not the seed's K = Q(sqrt(-7)).
findings.why_relevant: These are GL1 (Dirichlet / finite-order Hecke) zero-free statements. The seed's obligations involve the GL2 L-functions L(E,s), L(E^{-7},s) at s=1 (Q36 needs L''(E,1) and an archimedean rank-2 formula; L(E^{-7},1) != 0 is already PROVED_COMPUTER_ASSISTED). No Dirichlet-character nonvanishing in Re s > 7/8 enters any lab chain (Kurihara witnesses, B.18, Fornea-Gehrmann, Skinner IMC). Hecke characters over Q(sqrt(-3)) would only matter for CM curves with CM by Z[omega]; the seed has no CM. Kill test K-GRADE: even the Lean claim is 'review: status: unchecked' (formalization.yaml line 1778) and the lab cannot run comparator on the clone, so the statements remain IMPORTED_PREPRINT-with-Lean-claim for the lab.

Repository-wide: 416 comparator .json/.lean pairs, 0 'sorry' tokens in OAI/*.lean, 0 real 'axiom' declarations (3 regex hits are doc-comments), toolchain leanprover/lean4:v4.34.1, mathlib pinned at d13f23b7.
findings.why_relevant: Answers task item (a) completely. None of these touches elliptic curves, Selmer groups, p-adic L-functions, heights or quaternion algebras, so none serves FIN, ORDER9, Q36, any Sha[p^infinity], #Sha(E^{-7}), lemma TH, or any cost reduction (Brandt enumeration, B.18 production symbols). Only the Gaussian-integer and cyclotomic-field infrastructure (GaussianInt, CyclotomicField 3, NumberField.RingOfIntegers, Mathlib DirichletCharacter.LFunction) is Mathlib-level reusable API, which the lab can take from Mathlib directly without the clone.

findings.why_relevant: Answers task item (c). For the lab's LEAN_CHECKED grading the potentially relevant third-party libraries are lana-agents/elliptic-curves (formal group of a Weierstrass curve, formal logarithm: the objects behind the p-adic/Tamagawa local terms at good and additive primes, e.g. the seed's I1* at 2 and type III at 4547), lana-agents/tate-curves-theta (Tate curves: the uniformization relevant at the seed's multiplicative primes 3, 2243, 5843), lana-agents/heights (Serre-type different bounds, modular j, integrality on curves: ingredients of Neron-Tate/naive height comparisons needed for a Lean statement of the regulator) and ClassFieldTheory (ray class groups / Artin map for K = Q(sqrt(-7)), h(K)=1). However (1) they are unavailable in this lab (not in the clone; fetching would be a dependency build the CLAUDE.md forbids starting just to exhaust the allowance; network fetch of GitHub repos is a separate decision for the user), (2) nothing in openai/math uses them, so their content, soundness and axiom footprint are unverified here, and (3) none contains Selmer groups, p-adic L-functions or Euler systems. Named as unavailable inputs rather than simulated. PrimeCert offers verified primality certificates; for the seed's primes 2243, 4547, 5843 Mathlib's norm_num suffices, so this is not a bottleneck.

findings.item: Grading constraints established by the catalogue itself: formalization.yaml 'status: scope: Partial progress.', 'automation: methods: - method: agent', 'review: status: unchecked' (lines 969-1778); lean/README.md: 'They are organized in a single large library, so we recommend compiling only small portions at a time'; ComparatorChallenges/README.md: verification requires installing comparator, landrun, lean4export and running 'lake update; lake exe cache get; lake env comparator ComparatorChallenges/<X>.json', which this lab must not execute from the clone. Each .json pins permitted_axioms to [propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice] and enable_nanoda false. The 2026-10-07 history entry adds '6 formalizations and 5 other additions ... 300 / 719 = ~42%'.
findings.why_relevant: Kill test K-GRADE: a statement in this tree is LEAN_CHECKED only for the exact formal statement and only once independently re-checked; the catalogue's own review status is 'unchecked' and the lab cannot build it here. So the correct lab grade for every openai/math Lean claim remains IMPORTED_PREPRINT (with a recorded, unverified Lean claim), and no claim about E's Sha, rank, or L-values could be sourced here even if one existed.
